paper_metadata.title: QUASI-BINARY ENCODING BASED QUANTUM ALTERNATING OPERATOR ANSATZ

experiments.description: Quasi-binary QAOA on a 6-stock NASDAQ portfolio instance, evaluated with Normal-QAOA and CVaR-QAOA under four parameter-scheduling methods across depths p=1,2,4,8,16.

algorithm.variant: QB-QAOA with hard-constraint quasi-binary encoding; evaluated with Normal-QAOA and CVaR-QAOA
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 1000 COBYLA iterations per parameter initialization; 20 random initializations for Sample20

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quasi-binary encoding; each integer variable xi with bounds [Li, Ui] is shifted to yi=xi-Li and encoded using up to 2 log2(Ui-Li+1) qubits; for the 6-stock instance with α=0.5 and bounds [-1,1], total qubits = 18.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize portfolio risk-return objective equivalent to 1/2 q w^T Σ w - w^T E under 1^T w = 1, with discrete bounded weights encoded as integers.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard-constraint QAOA using a custom mixer (ring XY + ring XYY) that preserves the sum constraint and bound constraints; no penalty terms.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Phase-separation Hamiltonian C constructed from the binary expansion of the quasi-binary variables; mixer Hamiltonian B given in Eq. (12) with XY and XYY terms.

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over six NASDAQ stocks.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Historical returns rates used as input; expected returns and covariance matrix computed from the price history.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Brute-force for optimal/worst solution reference; COBYLA for parameter optimization
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute expected returns, covariance matrix, risk factor q, and feasible initial state via greedy allocation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Decode measured bitstrings to portfolio weights; compute cost distributions, approximation ratio, and cumulative distribution curves.

results.uncertainty: 95% CI over 33 repeats; exact interval not numerically specified
95% CI over 33 repeats; exact interval not numerically specified

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit computational speedup claim is made; the paper reports improved solution quality and discusses barren plateau behavior.

experiments.description: Mixability study of the quasi-binary mixer on a two-asset portfolio subproblem, measuring state-to-state reachability as QAOA depth increases.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two assets NVDA and TSLA, each represented by 6 qubits in quasi-binary encoding (two 1-qubits, one 2-qubit, two 4-qubits, one 8-qubit).
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Mixer-only feasibility-preserving evolution under the sum constraint y_NVDA + y_TSLA = 20.

problem_instance.description: Two-asset feasibility/mixability instance extracted from the 6-stock portfolio setup.

dataset_specification.date_range: same source as main NASDAQ dataset; not separately specified
dataset_specification.preprocessing: Bounds set to [-1,1], precision alpha fixed at 0.1, giving Ri=20 for each asset.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Enumerate feasible encodings and estimate mixability via discrete beta grid search.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute M_p(|ψ⟩,|ϕ⟩) as maximum overlap over sampled beta values and threshold the result to form grayscale maps.

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a mixer mixability study; no classical baseline or speedup claim is reported.

experiments.description: Instance 2: CVaR-QAOA on randomly selected Chinese stock portfolios with varying bounds and precision, evaluated across four parameter schedules and depths p=1,2,4,8,16.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not explicitly stated; COBYLA used for parameter optimization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quasi-binary encoding with hard constraints; cases requiring more than 20 total qubits were excluded.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Portfolio optimization objective in Markowitz form, minimizing risk-return tradeoff under budget and bound constraints.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard-constraint mixer preserving feasibility; no penalty terms.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Phase-separation Hamiltonian C and mixer Hamiltonian B as defined for QB-QAOA.

problem_instance.description: Randomly sampled stock-pool portfolio instances from the Chinese Shenzhen and Shanghai stock markets.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Chinese Shenzhen and Shanghai Stock Exchange Securities Market

dataset_specification.ticker_symbols: Randomly selected 4-8 stocks from 4836 stocks with no unknown values
dataset_specification.preprocessing: Upper and lower bounds for each stock randomly set between 0 and 1; interval between bounds randomly chosen from {0.1, 0.2, 0.4}; instances exceeding 20 qubits excluded.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Brute-force for approximation-ratio reference; COBYLA for quantum parameter optimization
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Random stock selection and bound assignment; compute feasible portfolio set under qubit cap.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximation ratio computed against brute-force optimal and worst costs; 320 experiments per configuration.

results.uncertainty: 95% CI over 320 experiments; exact interval not numerically specified
95% CI over 320 experiments; exact interval not numerically specified

speedup_claims.caveats: No runtime or speedup comparison is reported; only approximation ratio versus brute-force reference is given.

experiments.description: Precision-increasing iterative QB-QAOA on the 6-stock NASDAQ instance, using repeated runs with progressively finer precision while keeping qubit count fixed.

algorithm.variant: QB-QAOA precision-increasing iterative method with CVaR-QAOA and IQAOA scheduling

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same quasi-binary encoding as the main portfolio experiment; qubit count held fixed across iterations while bounds are shrunk around the previous solution.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Same portfolio optimization objective as Instance 1.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard-constraint mixer; iterative shrinking of bounds around the previous solution to refine precision.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Same QB-QAOA phase-separation and mixer Hamiltonians.

problem_instance.description: Iterative refinement of the six-stock NASDAQ portfolio instance from Instance 1.

dataset_specification.preprocessing: Start from coarse precision and iteratively reduce alpha while updating bounds around the previous solution; all six experiments used 18 qubits.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Brute-force reference for cost distribution comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate new bounds around previous solution at each iteration.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare cumulative distribution probability of solution costs across six precision levels.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims improved solution quality across iterations, not computational speedup.
